ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Ernest Shackleton

code.originalText: Four-month review before departure: exercise test, lipids, HbA1c, and the expedition medical plan

text.paragraph: Pre-departure review: exercise test and expedition medical plan. [S]

Mr. Shackleton returns nine days before his expedition sails, after a symptom-limited exercise test this morning. He has had no chest pain since the stent, has completed 18 sessions of cardiac rehabilitation, and walks briskly every day. The back strain from two weeks ago has settled with heat and acetaminophen, and he has delegated the lifting. He has not smoked for sixteen weeks and takes varenicline. He drinks two drinks at most, on four evenings a week. He takes aspirin, clopidogrel, atorvastatin, ezetimibe, and metoprolol daily. He wants to know what to carry and what to do if his heart gives trouble at sea. [S]

list.item:
Chronic coronary disease after a stent, angina-free (I25.118). Exercise treadmill test this morning: 11 minutes of the Bruce protocol, about 12.8 METs, stopped for fatigue, with no angina, no ischemic ST changes, no arrhythmia, and a normal blood pressure response. LDL cholesterol 44 mg/dL on atorvastatin and ezetimibe (total 108, HDL 45, triglycerides 95 mg/dL), a 74% reduction and at target. Blood pressure 120/76. Dr. Solberg-Adebayo agrees that he is fit to sail with the plan below; no routine surveillance imaging is needed. [S]
Expedition plan: written cardiac summary with ECG, stent card, and medicine list; six months of medicines plus three months' extra, split between two bags; clopidogrel stop date six months after the stent, written on the summary; aspirin for life.
An automated external defibrillator, aspirin, nitroglycerin, and emergency cardiac medicines on board; a satellite link to the cardiology team; and an evacuation plan to the nearest cardiac centers at the ports on the route.
Cold stress: warm up before heavy work, cover the face in cold wind, layer clothing, and avoid sudden maximal effort in the cold, which raises blood pressure and the heart's demand.
Chest pain that lasts more than 5 minutes after one nitroglycerin, or pain at rest: stop, take nitroglycerin, and get the ship's medical team and the satellite link at once.
Influenza vaccine given today.

Prediabetes (R73.03). HbA1c 5.7%, down from 5.9%, with weight down 3 kg. [S]
HbA1c on his return.

Nicotine dependence, in early remission (F17.210). Abstinent for sixteen weeks. [S]
Varenicline to 24 weeks; enough on board.
No cigarettes in the ship's stores for him; a plan for cravings at sea.

Alcohol use within limits. AUDIT-C 3, below the threshold for men. [S]
Keep to two drinks a day at most at sea.
